# Agustin Diaz-Cano - Software Engineer

## About

Software Engineer | Python Developer with 4+ years of experience in software development, specializing in AI/ML and Backend Development (Python).

I'm currently pursuing an M.Sc. in Information Systems Engineering at UTN, focused on Artificial Intelligence and Data Analysis. My thesis investigates LLM-guided reinforcement learning for legged robot navigation, benchmarked in MuJoCo and grid-based environments. My technical focus is building backend architectures that integrate GenAI in production-realistic conditions, not just prototypes. I'm developing projects with Python, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to explore LLM orchestration and AI agent design.

Previously, Sole QA Owner and quality authority for Grupo GDU's e-commerce platforms. Responsible for the entire quality strategy of web and mobile across multiple high-traffic sites, covering a multi-million dollar online channel with hundreds of thousands of users. Held full Go/No-Go authority on production releases with no dedicated QA team. During my tenure, the platforms—previously unranked—achieved nominations for the eCommerce Awards Uruguay in 2024 and 2025.

Transitioned from zero coding background in the pre-AI era. Wrote my first line of code in November 2020, received a job offer on May 14, 2021, and shipped my first production PR in June 2021 at an international fintech. Participated in more than 10 projects that reached production.

In game development, I created full modifications for the Men of War series as a solo developer, reaching over 200,000 downloads. Only a small percentage of Steam games, mods, and mobile apps (typically under 2-5%, and often closer to 1% for the 100k threshold) ever reach that level of adoption.

## Projects
[View All Projects](https://www.agustindiazcano.com/projects)

- **[MCP Transactional Agent](https://github.com/agustindiazcano/mcp-transactional-agent) (2026)**: Agentic MCP engine and RAG gateway. Asynchronous workflow engine that runs LLM agents against transactional business logic (refunds, fraud checks), built around one question: how much of an AI system's decisions can be deterministic and auditable. LLMs evaluate; only deterministic code executes side effects.
    - Stack: Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, pgvector, RabbitMQ, Docker, MCP, LangChain, Langfuse, Streamlit, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Google Cloud (Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Secret Manager), Vertex AI.
    - Security: the MCP server is the only path to side-effecting tools (token auth, per-tool authorization, sliding-window rate limiting, fail-closed audit log, prompt-injection test). Data integrity via idempotency keys, pessimistic row locking (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) and async queues. Chaos test (2,000 claims, worker killed twice, RabbitMQ restarted mid-run): zero lost messages, zero double refunds.
    - Decisions: Prompt Guard pre-filter plus an Asymmetric Double LLM-as-a-Judge (Gemini + GPT-OSS) with a Supreme Court cascade for tie-breaking. RAG over business rules with pgvector and provider-agnostic embeddings. Provider factory (OpenAI, Gemini, Vertex AI, Bedrock, Groq, mock). End-to-end Langfuse tracing with PII masking.
    - Quality and deploy: 300 tests (245 unit, 55 integration), 86% coverage gated in CI. Locust load test: P95 87 ms at 45+ req/s, zero failures, ~$0.0004 per transaction. Deployed on Google Cloud with Terraform and GitHub Actions through Workload Identity Federation (no stored keys).
- **[TestMind AI: Multi-Agent Mutation Testing System (MCP)](https://github.com/agustindiazcano/ibm-bob-mcp-agent-guard) (2026)**: Built from scratch in 48 hours for the IBM Bob 2.0 Hackathon (one of 1,124 successful submissions out of 3,464 teams and 15,727 participants). Measures whether tests actually catch bugs (not just line coverage), then uses AI agents to write the missing ones. Custom AST mutation engine, parallel multi-agent swarm (Writer + Critic + Gate), native MCP server, 30+ automated verification checks as guardrails against LLM hallucinations and cheating tests. ~20,000+ lines written in a single weekend.
    - Stack: Python, FastAPI, Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Docker, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Google Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Vercel, MCP, Vertex AI (Gemini), IBM watsonx.ai, Playwright.
    - [Live Demo](https://ibm-bob-mcp-agent-guard.vercel.app/) | [Video Demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m64qdd1axV0&t=6s) | [Hackathon Certificate](https://lablab.ai/u/@agustin_diazcano6/ai-hackathons/ibm-bob-2-hackathon/certificate)
- **[Quantum Computing: Windfarm Optimization (QWind)](https://github.com/agustindiazcano/qwind-qaoa-windfarm) (2026)**: Constraint-preserving XY-mixer QAOA for wind farm curtailment, executed on a real quantum computer (IonQ Forte 1). Chooses exactly K active turbines out of N (search space C(N, K)) by minimizing a wake-physics cost Hamiltonian with a variational circuit that preserves the number of active turbines by symmetry.
    - Stack: Python, Qiskit 2.5, QAOA, QUBO, Ising Hamiltonians, NumPy, SciPy (COBYLA), Pytest (150+ tests), GitHub Actions, ERA5 / Open-Meteo API, SCADA wind datasets (Zenodo).
    - [Live](https://agustindiazcano.github.io/qwind-qaoa-windfarm/) | [Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UGVkgYGXkF4) | [Repository](https://github.com/agustindiazcano/qwind-qaoa-windfarm) | [Qollab](https://qollab.xyz/u/agustindiazcano/qwind)
- **[Argentina 2056: Data Visualization and Economic Analysis](https://github.com/agustindiazcano/arg-2056-udesa) (2026)**: Macroeconomic data visualization platform and 3D geospatial viewer of the 1817 Andes crossing. [Live Demo](https://argentina2056.vercel.app/)
    - Stack: TypeScript, React, Vite, Zustand, Three.js, ECharts, MapLibre GL, GSAP, Python, NumPy, jsonschema, pytest, Vitest, Playwright, axe, GitHub Actions, Vercel.
    - Data pipeline: automated Python ingestion from the World Bank (REST), IMF (SDMX) and Argentine Secretariats of Energy/Agriculture (CKAN), normalized to constant 2015 USD; manual extraction from official PDFs (INDEC, Mining Secretariat) with automated integrity tests. The frontend has zero hardcoded numbers: it only consumes versioned JSON datasets, keeping traceability of sources, dates and units.
- **[Anti-Fragile Agentic Workflow (AFAW)](https://github.com/agustindiazcano/afaw-anti-fragile-agentic-workflow) (2026)**: Boilerplate and rules for AI-assisted development with multiple parallel coding agents (Claude, Gemini, etc.). Premise: the AI decides, the engine measures. Every result is verified with deterministic tools (tests, type checkers, AST mutation testing, CI) and a human approves every PR; rules are enforced outside the prompt (branch protection, hooks, CI). Isolated per-agent state checked by CI, strict TDD, one branch per task, cloud validation in GitHub Actions. Reference rules target a Python backend (`mypy --strict`) and can be adapted to other stacks.
- **[AI Crypto Trading Agent](https://github.com/agustindiazcano/algorithmic-trading-engine) (2025)**: Quantitative Binance trading system evolving from rule-based scripts into a service-oriented decision-making agent: real-time market ingestion, technical-signal scoring (MACD/DEA, Bollinger, ADX, RSI, ATR), risk management and order execution. Phased roadmap (Postgres/Redis/Docker, backtesting-driven calibration, RAG-based sentiment, genetic-algorithm strategy optimization), each phase gated behind empirical validation. Stack: Python, WebSockets, Binance API, PostgreSQL, Redis. Currently in simulation mode (`REAL_TRADES=False`) with an openly tracked 18-item known-bugs log.
- **[Memory-Constrained LLM Optimization: OpenAI Parameter Golf](https://github.com/agustindiazcano/openai-llm-optimizers-parameter-golf) (2026, repo under construction)**: Participation in OpenAI's 16MB Parameter Golf Challenge: training LLMs under extreme 16MB memory constraints with custom optimizers. Over two weeks of experiments on RunPod H100 GPU clusters with $200+ invested in compute. Stack: Python, PyTorch, RunPod.
- **[Zombie Horde Survivors](https://github.com/agustindiazcano/zombie-horde-survivors) (2026)**: Hybrid 3D squad shooter and real-time strategy (RTS) web game that runs in the browser with no server or accounts. Four soldiers and a support drone fight dynamic waves of zombies and bosses, playable in third person, top-down or RTS command view, with drag-and-drop inventory, motion tracker radar, perks, between-wave shop and mobile support (touch, gyroscope, adaptive layout). [Play Online](https://agustindiazcano.github.io/zombie-horde-survivors/)
    - Architecture: the whole simulation (`src/sim`) is pure TypeScript, free of rendering dependencies (enforced by ESLint and Vitest), running at a fixed 60 Hz step with seeded randomness, connected to Three.js (WebGL, GLSL shaders for water, sky and weather) through frame interpolation. All gameplay numbers live in validated JSON (zod). 3D asset licenses are verified in CI.
    - Stack: TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, GLSL, zod, Vitest, ESLint, Prettier, Rapier (deterministic Rust/WASM physics, used for the map 12 physics lab: balls, boxes, ragdolls), Rust + wasm-bindgen + wasm-pack (`crates/sim-core`: zombie separation and flow field in the game, ocean compared only), GitHub Pages and GitHub Actions, Steam planned.
    - Custom physics: O(1) constant-time collisions and gravity unified in a single solver. On top of it, fluids (waves, vortices, buoyancy) and optics (reflections, refraction, caustics, fog) are drawn with lightweight formulas in a single pass instead of heavy render passes. Used for game movement and collisions and for the water and light of the sea and sky (map 13).
- **[M.Sc. Thesis, AI/ML Research](https://github.com/agustindiazcano/msc-thesis-neurosymbolic-llm-rl-navigation) (2026 to present)**: LLM-guided reinforcement learning for legged robot navigation (UTN). Hierarchical neuro-symbolic architecture: an RBF-based perceptual layer generates interpretable concept activations, and an LLM resolves navigation decisions only in ambiguous cases where multiple concepts compete. Currently benchmarking RBF vs. MLP policies (curriculum learning, grid-based navigation) before full integration in MuJoCo.
- **Astrophysics Data Simulations (2023)**: Robust simulations modeling complex astrophysics systems.
- **LATAM E-commerce Ecosystem (2022)**: Scalable and localized e-commerce solution handling complex gateways.
- **InsurTech Quoting Engine (2021)**: Real-time insurance premium quoting engine.
- **Crypto Ethereum Mining Rig (2017)**: Assembled and configured a rig for Ethereum mining in the early adoption era. [View Repository](https://github.com/agustindiazcano/eth-mining-infrastructure-2017)
- **Game Dev: Modding Ecosystem (2010)**: 220,000+ Downloads across Men of War series (solo creator, no marketing budget, no pre-existing audience).
    - [Men of War Zombie Mod Main (+113k Downloads)](https://www.moddb.com/mods/zombie-mod5)
    - [Men of War Zombie Mod Assault (+84k Downloads)](https://www.moddb.com/mods/men-of-war-zombie-mod)
    - [Men of War HD Mod (20k Downloads)](https://www.moddb.com/mods/hd-mod)
    - [Zombie Mod Men of War Grokipedia](https://grokipedia.com/page/Zombie_Mod_Men_of_War)

    **Context (actual rarity)**:  
    - Only ~1–2% of Steam games ever reach 100,000+ lifetime units.  
    - On Google Play, ~75% of newly launched apps never exceed 1,000 downloads, and only ~2% surpass 100,000.  
    - On the App Store (iOS), ~92–93% of apps show effectively zero measurable downloads.  
    - The majority of mid-size company apps (and many corporate products) never reach 200k organic downloads.  
    Achieving 220k+ downloads as a solo creator is a long-tail outcome that 98–99% of software engineers never accomplish independently in their entire careers.

    Sources:  
    - Steam: https://www.steampageanalyzer.com/blog/average-steam-game-sales · https://gamalytic.com/years · https://x.com/WladMarhulets/status/1920197804275667122  
    - Android: https://www.appbrain.com/stats/android-app-downloads · https://www.statista.com/statistics/269884/android-app-downloads/ · https://x.com/Similarweb/status/2066064899428483162  
    - iOS: https://getappniche.com/answers/how-many-downloads-is-good

### Knowledge-Based Systems & Fuzzy Logic Project
**Course**: Intelligent Data Exploitation, UTN MSc (November 2024)
An Artificial Intelligence project applying classical knowledge-based systems methodology (METHONTOLOGY), rule-based inference, and fuzzy logic to reduce false positives in bug report triage for an e-commerce platform. Contributed as the domain expert consulted during the knowledge acquisition process.
